final_state.description: High-fidelity linear SOC clinical reasoning simulator for OASIS-E2 assessment coding. RNs navigate 27 patient artifacts across the full care continuum (Hospital → SNF → ALF → Home Health SOC) to extract evidence, select correct OASIS codes, defend rationale selections, and link supporting documentation. Single canonical patient case (Evelyn Vance, 82F, CHF/DM2).

Evidence extraction via highlight-to-save interaction
Evidence validation engine with artifact-to-item mapping
Three-phase remediation engine (QUIZ → REVIEW → SUCCESS)
Audio narration system (233 WAV files via Qwen3-TTS)
Linear section progression enforcement (Disclosure → A-O → Final Review)
Conflict detection prompts with toast notifications
SCORM 1.2 / xAPI / LTI completion tracking

product_ideation.label: Inferred — Not from source files
product_ideation.problem: Registered Nurses in home health consistently miscategorize OASIS-E2 assessment items due to inability to reconcile fragmented clinical documentation across care transitions (Hospital → SNF → ALF → Home Health). This drives coding errors, compliance audit failures, and reimbursement discrepancies under PDGM.
product_ideation.value: Transforms abstract OASIS coding guidelines into experiential clinical reasoning through artifact-based evidence extraction. Improves coding accuracy, reduces audit risk, and builds defensible documentation habits.
use_cases: New-hire RN onboarding to OASIS-E2 SOC assessment
Remediation training for RNs with high coding error rates
Pre-survey competency validation for QA teams
Annual competency refresh for experienced clinicians

ux_design.label: Inferred — Not from source files
ux_design.strategy: Linear guided SOC flow with split-workspace architecture mirrors real-world EHR patterns. Three-column layout reduces context-switching between chart review and assessment coding. Progressive disclosure prevents cognitive overload by revealing one section at a time.
ux_design.workflow_reasoning: Sequential section progression mirrors actual SOC visit documentation workflow. Evidence extraction interaction (highlight-to-save) builds muscle memory for artifact reconciliation patterns used in production EHR systems.
ux_design.cognitive_load_strategy: Sticky section anchors, collapsed inactive sections, linear lock enforcement, and audio narration all serve to constrain decision space and reduce extraneous cognitive load per Sweller's Cognitive Load Theory.
ux_design.interaction_constraints: No skip-ahead, no field re-editing after correct answer, audio completion required before progression

SOC-specific clinical reasoning under documentation constraints
competency_levels: Recognition: Identify relevant evidence in artifacts
Application: Select correct OASIS code from evidence
Analysis: Defend rationale against trap options
Synthesis: Link multiple artifacts to support coding decision
training_model.assessment_model: Per-item quiz with 5-option rationale selection + evidence linking validation. Incorrect answers trigger targeted remediation audio. Retry mechanism resets only incorrect fields. Final review aggregates performance.

simulation_strategy.label: Inferred — Not from source files
simulation_strategy.description: Single canonical patient case (Evelyn Vance, 82F) traced across complete care continuum. 27 artifacts with varying reliability levels create realistic documentation reconciliation challenge. Conflicting information across artifacts forces critical analysis.
simulation_strategy.use_of_conflict: Trap rationales include common real-world coding errors: relying on historical records over SOC findings, proxy report weighting, single-source acceptance, narrative term matching without functional assessment, and incomplete interview handling.
simulation_strategy.decision_complexity_detail: Each OASIS item requires multi-step reasoning: extract evidence → assess reliability → reconcile conflicts → select code → defend rationale → link supporting artifacts

narration_strategy.tone: Professional clinical educator. Authoritative but supportive. Uses CMS terminology precisely. Explains 'why' behind correct coding, not just 'what'.

governing_rules.description: CMS-485 training enforces one continuous clinical story: Face-to-Face Encounter → OASIS Assessment → Plan of Care → Visit Notes → Billing. No standalone field instruction without clinical narrative context.
